finding3: ALLEGATION 3: Did Marcus Doyle make remarks about religion, or about Goldberg's religious observance, in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, including at or after the team huddle (which the complainant gives as September 9, 2026)? FINDING: SUBSTANTIATED. First, the September 9 huddle. Leah Goldberg ("Goldberg"), Member Services Representative II, stated that when Marcus Doyle ("Doyle"), Team Supervisor, Member Services, was going over the rotation and someone asked about requests, he said "Fine." and then, looking directly at her, said "We'll see about Fridays." 1 2 Jordan Kim ("Kim"), Member Services Representative, who attended the huddle, independently recalled Doyle saying something like "Fine" and then "we'll see about Fridays." 3 4 Doyle did not deny the remark, answering "Probably" when asked whether he said it. 5 6 The remark was made five days after Goldberg's September 4 email asking to be kept off Friday shifts after 5 PM because she observes Shabbat, and while that request was unanswered. 7 8 In that setting, a remark about Fridays directed at Goldberg was a remark about her Friday religious observance. Doyle's explanation was that he meant they would see how the rotation worked out and that it "wasn't aimed at Leah." 6 Goldberg, however, stated that "Everyone knew what he meant." 2 Second, the "holy day" remark. Kim stated that after the huddle Doyle was at his desk, speaking loudly, and said, "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays." Kim said he heard this himself from about six feet away. 9 Goldberg did not hear the remark and learned of it from Kim, so her account is second-hand. 10 Kim's first-hand account is the basis for the finding. Doyle did not deny it, stating that he "might have said something like that" and that it "was about staffing in general, not about Leah." 11 Doyle's account therefore confirms the substance of the remark and disputes only its purpose. The remark expressly refers to a "holy day" and was made about Friday staffing under the Q4 rotation, so it is a remark about religion in connection with the rotation whatever its intended target. Third, the surrounding conduct. The same week, Kim posted a swap offer in the team chat and tagged Doyle, who reacted with a thumbs up. 12 Doyle then denied Goldberg's request on September 14 in a one-sentence email. 8 Doyle stated that he saw the offer and did not pursue it. 13 Against that sequence, the two remarks are consistent with one another and with the way the request was handled. They are not stray comments unrelated to Goldberg's Friday request. On the totality of the evidence, Doyle's accounts of both remarks are partial admissions that Kim's and Goldberg's accounts corroborate. His explanations go to what he meant, and the words and the context show that they concerned Goldberg's religious observance and the Friday rotation. Thus, based on a preponderance of the evidence, it is likely that Doyle made remarks about religion, and about Goldberg's religious observance, in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, at and after the September 9 huddle. Note: I left out the reported "find a job that fits her religion" remark. Kim heard it only from Rivera, Rivera says she told Kim only that Doyle had been "grumbling about the Friday requests," and Doyle denies it. 14 15 16 Also, the findings recorded in the file show this allegation as "Partly found" and the Anti-Harassment Policy as not substantiated, so the file will need updating if you adopt this finding.I drafted it as your finding.

harassment: The argument: Even taken at face value, a single overheard remark about staffing doesn't meet the policy's definition of harassment. Severity or pervasiveness. The policy defines harassment as unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that is "sufficiently severe or pervasive to create an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment, or that affects the terms and conditions of employment." 1 The record shows one remark, with no slur, threat or name-calling. Nothing shows a pattern of religious comments. - Not directed at her. Kim says Doyle was "at his desk talking to himself", and quotes the words as "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays." 2 Goldberg did not hear it and learned of it from Kim. 3 A remark made to no one, and relayed second-hand, is hard to call intimidating toward her. - Plausible neutral meaning. Doyle says he "might have said something like that" and that it "was about staffing in general, not about Leah." 4 Read that way, it is a complaint about coverage, which fits the rotation context, and Doyle said nothing about Goldberg's own observance. Not the other remark. The "find a job that fits her religion" remark would be far more serious, but it rests on Kim's account of what Rivera told him. Kim didn't hear it, Doyle denies it, and Rivera says she told Kim only that Doyle had been "grumbling about the Friday requests." 5 6 7 So the strongest version keeps the case confined to the "holy day" remark alone. - Accommodation decision is a different allegation. Whatever Doyle's tone, the failure to discuss alternatives is already covered by Allegation 2, so the remark doesn't need to carry that weight. Where it is weakest. Kim heard the remark first-hand from about six feet away, and Doyle doesn't deny it. 2 4 It came the same day as "We'll see about Fridays" said while looking at Goldberg, and about a week before a denial with no discussion of options. 8 9 A reader could see a pattern of dismissiveness toward Friday requests rather than a stray comment. This is one side of the argument.I've given the strongest case for you above, along with where it's weakest.

Leah Goldberg ("Goldberg"), Member Services Representative II, stated that while Marcus Doyle ("Doyle"), Team Supervisor, Member Services, was going over the rotation and someone asked about requests, he said "Fine." and then, looking at her, said "We'll see about Fridays." 1 Jordan Kim ("Kim"), Member Services Representative, who attended the huddle, recalled Doyle saying something like "Fine" and then "we'll see about Fridays." 2 Doyle answered "Probably" when asked whether he said it, explained that he meant they would see how the rotation worked out, and stated that it "wasn't aimed at Leah." 3 Goldberg's September 4 email asking to be kept off Friday shifts after 5 PM because she observes Shabbat had been sent five days earlier. 4 Coming in that setting, the remark concerned her Friday observance, and Doyle's account of what he meant does not change what was said. Second, the "holy day" remark. Kim stated that after the huddle Doyle was at his desk, talking loudly, and said, "If everyone wanted their holy day off, nobody would work Fridays." Kim said he heard it himself from about six feet away. 5 Goldberg did not hear it and learned of it from Kim, so her account of it is second-hand. 6 Doyle stated that he "might have said something like that" and that it was about staffing in general. 7 His account confirms the substance of the remark and disputes only its purpose. The words refer expressly to a "holy day" and were spoken about Friday staffing under the Q4 rotation, so they are a remark about religion in connection with the rotation. Third, the reported "find a job" remark is not part of what occurred on this record. Kim said he heard it only from Carla Rivera ("Rivera"), Workforce Management Analyst, and not himself. 8 Rivera said she heard no remark by Doyle about Goldberg's religion and told Kim only that Doyle had been "grumbling about the Friday requests." 9 Doyle denied saying it. 10 The finding does not rest on this remark. Severity and pervasiveness. Whether the remarks were made is a separate question from whether the conduct was severe or pervasive, and the finding answers the first. The Anti-Harassment Policy defines harassment as unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic that is sufficiently severe or pervasive to create an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, or that affects the terms and conditions of employment. 11 The established conduct is two remarks on a single day, one at the huddle and one afterwards at Doyle's desk. 2 5 Goldberg heard no other religious comment from Doyle herself. 6 She stated that she does not feel her religion is respected on the team. 12 Doyle stated that he is not against anyone's religion. 13 The finding is therefore that Doyle made the remarks, and it is not a finding that they met the policy's severe-or-pervasive threshold. On the totality of the evidence, Doyle partly admitted both remarks, and Goldberg's and Kim's accounts corroborate them. His explanations go to meaning and purpose, and the words and context show that the remarks concerned the Friday rotation and religious observance. Thus, based on a preponderance of the evidence, it is likely that Doyle made remarks about religion, and about Goldberg's religious observance, in connection with the Q4 Friday rotation, at and after the September 9 huddle.
